text:
Mia: heads-up, grafana alert firing for telemetry pipeline p99 CPU across ingest nodes since last deploy (1756788800). saw a sharp jump around 1756788905.
Sam: ugh. which change was rolled at 1756788900?
Oliver: that was the agent serializer refactor (PR #4287) — switched to zero-copy buffer but added span->proto conversion step earlier.
Mia: hmm could be CPU from serialization churn. p99 went from 220ms to 610ms on encoder hotspot.
Julia: dropping a quick flame link: https://grafana.internal/r/ai1XqP/flame?run=1756789000
Sam: looked at flame — lots of time in `SpanSerializer::to_proto` and `string::reserve` calls. memory copies spiking.
Ken: did batching config change too? smaller batches -> more per-span overhead.
Mia: no explicit batching change in config. but rollout toggled `agent.batch_flush_ms` to 25ms in canary to reduce latency.
Oliver: ah, smaller flush window + the new serializer can increase syscall/alloc frequency.
telemetry-bot: alert: telemetry.ingest.cpu.p99 > 75% for cluster-ingest-west for 3m
Julia: can we simulate by replaying 30m of traces against current branch with both serializers? i can run an A/B with synthetic load.
Sam: quick idea: revert `reserve` path in serializer to reuse buffers from a pool. that should cut alloc churn.
Ken: also consider increasing `batch_flush_ms` back to 200ms for the canary, see if p99 drops — tradeoff on tail latency but saves CPU.
Mia: agree. I prefer testing buffer-pool fix first, then a config rollback if needed. less user-facing change.
Oliver: code snippet I ran locally:
```
// reuse buffer
let mut buf = BUF_POOL.get().unwrap();
buf.clear();
span.serialize_into(&mut buf);
exporter.send(buf);
BUF_POOL.put(buf);
```
reduced allocations by ~40% in microbench.
Julia: nice. can you open a patch? i'll wire up a canary flag so deploys can toggle serializer variant at runtime.
Sam: we should also add a dashboard tile showing per-second allocs and batch-size distribution — helps correlate.
Mia: filed ticket INF-952 for dashboard + alloc metrics.
Oliver: rolling a canary with buffer-pool to 5% now. deploy-bot: canary rollout started for service=telemetry-ingest, canary=5%
deploy-bot: canary health OK at 60s
Mia: after 10m, p99 CPU dropped from 82% -> 36% on canary slice. great.
Ken: sounds promising. what's the impact on p99 latency?
Julia: latency p99 improved from 610ms -> 270ms in canary. batch sizes slightly higher but within SLA.
Sam: next steps: merge buffer-pool fix, add dashboard panels, create a transient rollout UX toggle so SREs can flip serializer fast. also convo about sampling: could we apply light head-based sampling pre-serialize for noisy routes?
Mia: sampling is on the table but it's a policy decision — opens routing/quotas discussion. for now we keep full fidelity.
Oliver: noted. i'll draft a small RFC on serializer pool + optional sampling hooks for product review.
Mia: thanks everyone. tagging infra to follow up on quota implications: @Ken @Sam :thumbsup:
Sam: 👍 will coordinate with quota team if sampling is proposed.
telemetry-bot: incident follow-up: created incident/1756789-serializer-cpu with initial notes
Mia: closing thread as canary looks stable, will monitor overnight and schedule rollback plan if regressions appear.
